feed.description: Software engineering conversations: reliability, architecture, delivery, and the tradeoffs nobody puts in the blog post.
feed.title: Practical Systems

bullets: Good on-call rotations are designed so waking up is rare, tying directly into how communication shapes reliability work.
A great RFC starts with context and constraints, then options — once internalized, the rest of the decisions get easier.
Writing things down turns disagreement into collaboration; the second-order effect is the part most people miss.
Postmortems that focus on individuals miss the system that made the mistake easy — blame the design, not the person.
Architecture decisions are mostly tradeoffs, and the framing matters because it tells you which tradeoffs you're making.
Risk management is a communication problem — surfacing constraints and options turns risk into a collaborative decision.
The failure mode of skipping written context is rebuilding the same system from scratch a year later.
A practical first step is picking one idea from the discussion and running it for two weeks; the rest is iteration.
